source.title: Some open problems in dynamical systems

accepted.question_text: Let P_α(z) = e^{2πiα} z + z^2, where α is an irrational real Bruno number, and let S_α be the maximal connected open neighborhood of 0 on which P_α is analytically linearizable. Does there exist a Bruno number α such that the boundary ∂S_α of this Siegel singular disk is a smooth C^∞ embedded circle in the complex plane?

evidence.quote: 1. Does there exist α1 a Bruno number such that ∂Sα1 (the boundary of Sα1 ) is a C∞ submanifold of C (a circle) ?

accepted.question_text: For the same quadratic polynomial family P_α(z) = e^{2πiα} z + z^2 with α a Bruno number and S_α the corresponding Siegel singular disk, does there exist a Bruno number α such that the boundary ∂S_α is not a Jordan curve?

evidence.quote: 2. Does there exist α2 a Bruno number such that ∂Sα2 (the boundary of Sα2 ) is not a Jordan curve ?

accepted.question_text: Fix α ∈ T^n satisfying a Diophantine condition. Let C^∞_0(T^n) be the space of smooth real-valued functions on T^n with Haar integral 0, and for ϕ in this space define the exact symplectic diffeomorphism F_ϕ on T^*T^n ≅ T^n × R^n by F_ϕ(θ,r) = (θ + r, r + ∂ϕ/∂θ(θ + r)). Let U_α be the set of ϕ for which F_ϕ leaves invariant a smooth torus T_{α,ϕ}, given as the graph of a smooth map ψ : T^n → R^n, and such that F_ϕ restricted to that torus is smoothly conjugate to the translation R_α : θ ↦ θ + α. Is the boundary ∂U_α, viewed inside C^∞(T^n), a locally flat C^k submanifold for some k ≥ 0?

evidence.quote: 2.1 - Question. Is the boundary ∂Uα of Uα in C∞ (Tn) a locally ﬂat Ck-submanifold (for some k≥0) ?

accepted.question_text: Let U = ⋃_{α∈DC} U_α, where for each Diophantine α ∈ T^n the set U_α consists of smooth zero-average functions ϕ on T^n for which the exact symplectic diffeomorphism F_ϕ(θ,r) = (θ + r, r + ∂ϕ/∂θ(θ + r)) preserves a smooth invariant torus on which the dynamics is smoothly conjugate to translation by α. What is the smallest real number k > 0 for which the union U is open near 0 in the C^k topology?

evidence.quote: 2.2 - Let ⋃ α∈DCUα = U ; what is the minimal number k∈R∗ + for which U is open near 0, in the Ck-topology ?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a real-analytic diffeomorphism of either the cylinder T^1 × [−1,1] or the sphere S^2 that is homotopic to the identity, preserves Lebesgue measure, has only finitely many periodic orbits, and nevertheless has a dense orbit?

evidence.quote: 3.1 - Question. Does there exist a Cω(= R-analytic)-diﬀeomorphism, homotopic to the identity, Lebesgue measure-preserving, of T1×[−1, 1] orS2, with a ﬁnite number of periodic orbits and a dense orbit ?

accepted.question_text: Let f be a smooth diffeomorphism of the cylinder T^1 × [−1,1] that preserves Lebesgue measure, is homotopic to the identity, has no periodic points, and whose boundary rotation number ρ(f|_{T^1×{−1}}) = α satisfies a Diophantine condition. Must f be smoothly C^∞-conjugate to the rigid cylinder rotation R_α(θ,r) = (θ + α, r)?

evidence.quote: 3.2 - Question. Letf be a C∞ -diﬀeomorphism preserving the Lebesgue measure of T1×[−1, 1], homotopic to the identity, that has a ﬁnite number of periodic points ... and is such that the rotation number ρ(f|T1×{−1}) = α satisﬁes a diophantine condition. Is f C∞ -conjugated to Rα(θ,r) = (θ+α,r) ?

accepted.question_text: Let f be a smooth Lebesgue-measure-preserving diffeomorphism of the closed unit disk D^2 = {z ∈ C : |z| ≤ 1} with only finitely many periodic points. Must f be smoothly C^∞-conjugate to the rigid rotation r_α(z) = e^{2πiα} z for some angle α?
accepted.context_brief: Disk rigidity with few periodic points

evidence.quote: We also ask the similar question for D2 ={z ∈ C,|z| ≤1}. When f is Lebesgue measure preserving and f has a ﬁnite number of periodic points is f C∞ -conjugated to rα ?

accepted.question_text: Let f : R^{2n} → R^{2n} be a germ of a real-analytic symplectic diffeomorphism fixing 0, with linear part symplectically conjugate to r_{α_1} × ··· × r_{α_n}, where α = (α_1, ..., α_n) satisfies a Diophantine condition. Does every sufficiently small neighborhood of 0 contain a positive-Lebesgue-measure set of invariant Lagrangian tori for f?

evidence.quote: 3.4 - Conjecture. If f is real analytic, then f leaves invariant, in any small neighbourhood of 0, a set of positive Lebesgue measure of Lagrangian tori .

accepted.question_text: Let G^∞_μ(D^2) be the group of smooth diffeomorphisms of the disk D^2 that are supported in D^2 and preserve normalized Lebesgue measure μ. Does every C^∞ neighborhood of the identity in G^∞_μ(D^2) contain a diffeomorphism g with positive metric entropy h_μ(g) > 0?

evidence.quote: 4.2 - Conjecture. For every C∞ -neighbourhoodW of the identity in G∞ µ there exists g∈W such that hµ(g)> 0.

accepted.question_text: For smooth Lebesgue-measure-preserving diffeomorphisms of the disk, let G be the set of maps f with λ_+(f,μ) = 0, equivalently zero metric entropy by the stated inequalities. Which of the two Baire alternatives holds: either G is a dense G_δ set, or there exists a nonempty C^∞-open set U on which every map has entropy bounded below by some δ > 0?

evidence.quote: 4.3 - One of the 2 exclusive possibilities is true by Baire category : a) The set G is a dense Gδ. b) There exists U⊂G∞ µ , a C∞ open set, U̸=∅, for every g∈U one has hµ(g)≥δ, for some δ >0. Question. Is a) or b) true ?

accepted.question_text: Let G^∞_*(M) denote either the space of smooth measure-preserving diffeomorphisms of a compact manifold M or the space of smooth symplectic diffeomorphisms, and let SE^∞_* be the class of diffeomorphisms with uniformly positive stable Lyapunov exponents along periodic orbits in the sense defined in the paper. Is the subset of maps in G^∞_*(M) that admit a dominated splitting on all of M C^1-dense in SE^∞_*?

evidence.quote: 4.9 - Questions. a) Is the set {f∈G∞ ∗ (M ),f has a dominated splitting on M}C1-dense in SE∞ ∗ ?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a connected simply connected manifold M^n that admits a partially hyperbolic diffeomorphism?

evidence.quote: b) Does there exist a connected and simply connected manifold Mn with a partially hyperbolic diﬀeomorphism ?

accepted.question_text: For the complement G^∞_*(M) \ SE^∞_* of the stably-exponent class inside the space of smooth conservative or symplectic diffeomorphisms, which of the two Baire alternatives from §4.3 holds: generic zero exponent/entropy behavior, or the existence of a nonempty open set with entropy uniformly bounded below?

evidence.quote: c) On G∞ ∗ (M )−SE∞ ∗ , which of the two possibilities of 4.3 is true ?

accepted.question_text: If f is a strictly ergodic smooth diffeomorphism of a compact connected manifold M^n, meaning that f is both minimal and uniquely ergodic, must the topological entropy of f be equal to 0?

evidence.quote: 4.10 - Let Mn be compact connected manifold and f a strictly ergodic C∞ -diﬀeomorphism (minimal (i.e. every orbit is dense) and uniquely ergodic). Conjecture. The topological entropy of f equals 0.

accepted.question_text: Let Diff^∞_0(T^n) be the group of smooth diffeomorphisms of the torus T^n that are smoothly isotopic to the identity, and let G be the C^∞ closure of the subset of maps with no periodic points. For n ≥ 2, does this closed set G have empty interior in Diff^∞_0(T^n)?

evidence.quote: 5.2 - Question. Does the closed set G have no interior (n≥2) in Diﬀ∞ 0 (Tn) ?

accepted.question_text: Let H_0(r) be a real-analytic strictly convex Hamiltonian on T^*T^n = T^n × R^n, with superlinear growth at infinity and ∂H_0/∂r(0) = 0. Can one find a real-analytic family H_ε(θ,r) = H_0(r) + ε H_1(θ,r,ε) and a small ε_0 such that, on the energy level H_{ε_0}^{-1}(1), the periodic orbits of the Hamiltonian flow are not dense?
accepted.context_brief: Analytic perturbation with sparse periodic orbits

evidence.quote: Question. Can one ﬁnd a Cω-familyHε(θ,r) = H0(r) +εH0(θ,r,ε), every thing being R-analytic, such that for some ε0 small on H−1 ε0 (1), the periodic orbits of the Hamiltonian ﬂow of Hε0 are not dense ?

accepted.question_text: For n ≥ 2, can one find a smooth compact connected hypersurface M^{2n−1} ⊂ R^{2n} whose characteristic flow is minimal, meaning that every orbit is dense in M^{2n−1}?

evidence.quote: 1. When n≥ 2 can one ﬁnd M 2n−1⊂ R2n, a C∞ -compact connected hypersurface, such that on M 2n−1 the characteristic ﬂow is minimal (every orbit is dense) ?

accepted.question_text: Can the characteristic flow on a smooth compact connected hypersurface M^{2n−1} ⊂ R^{2n} be an Anosov flow?

evidence.quote: 2. Can the characteristic ﬂow on M 2n−1 be an Anosov ﬂow ?

accepted.question_text: Let M^n be a compact connected oriented manifold of dimension n ≥ 3 with Euler characteristic χ(M^n) = 0, equipped with a smooth volume form Ω. In every homotopy class of nowhere-vanishing smooth Ω-divergence-free vector fields X on M^n, does there exist such an X whose flow has no periodic orbit?

evidence.quote: 5.7 - Questions. a) Does there exist vector ﬁelds as above (in every homotopy class of non-zero vector ﬁelds) such that the ﬂow of fX t has no periodic orbit ?

accepted.question_text: Under the same assumptions on a compact oriented manifold M^n with χ(M^n)=0 and a nowhere-vanishing smooth Ω-divergence-free vector field X, does there exist such a vector field whose flow is Ω-ergodic?

evidence.quote: b) Does there exist vector-ﬁelds as above such that the ﬂow fX t is Ω-ergodic ?

accepted.question_text: Let (M^{2n},ω) be a compact symplectic manifold with Euler characteristic χ(M^{2n}) = 0 that does not fiber over S^1. Does every symplectic diffeomorphism of (M^{2n},ω) that is homotopic to the identity have at least one fixed point, and in fact at least as many fixed points as the minimal number of zeros of any symplectic vector field on M^{2n}?
accepted.context_brief: Fixed points on non-fibered symplectic manifold

evidence.quote: Conjecture. Every symplectic diﬀeomorphism homotopic to the identity o f (M 2n,w ), where χ(M 2n) = 0 and M 2n does not ﬁber over S1, has a ﬁxed point (in fact a number of ﬁxed points ≥ minimal number of zeros of any symplectic vector-ﬁeld) .

accepted.question_text: For n ≥ 3, can one find a smooth Hamiltonian H in a sufficiently small C^k neighborhood (with k ≥ 2) of the integrable Hamiltonian H_0(r) = ½\|r\|^2 on T^*T^n such that the Hamiltonian flow of H on the energy hypersurface H^{-1}(1) has at least one dense orbit?

evidence.quote: 6.2 - Questions. 1. Can one ﬁnd an example of a C∞ -Hamiltonian H in a small Ck-neighbourhoodk≥ 2 of H0(r) = 1/2∥r∥2 such that, on H−1(1), the Hamiltonian ﬂow of H has one dense orbit ?

accepted.question_text: For a C^∞-generic Hamiltonian H near the integrable model on T^*T^n and for a generic ergodic minimizing measure μ in the sense of Mather, is the restricted flow f^H_t|_{supp(μ)} on H^{-1}(1) hyperbolic?

evidence.quote: 2. For the C∞ -generic H and the generic ergodic minimal measure µ of Mather [MA2], is the ﬂow fH t|supp(µ) on H−1(1) a hyperbolic ﬂow ?

accepted.question_text: For a C^∞-generic Hamiltonian H on H^{-1}(1), are the invariant probability measures supported on periodic orbits dense, in the weak topology, in the set of ergodic minimizing measures?

evidence.quote: 3. For the C∞ -generic H on H−1(1) are the probability measures deﬁned by periodic orbits, dense (in the weak topology on probability measures) in the ergodic minimal measures ?

accepted.question_text: For a C^∞-generic Hamiltonian H, can one find a closed connected invariant set F ⊂ H^{-1}(1) that contains the supports of all ergodic minimizing measures, has the property that orbits asymptotic to locally minimizing orbits are dense in F, and also carries a dense orbit of the Hamiltonian flow itself?

evidence.quote: 4. Can one ﬁnd C∞ -generically a closed connected set F , invariant by the Hamiltonian ﬂow fH t of H, F⊂H−1(1), such that F contains all the supports of the ergodic minimal measures, in F the orbits asymptotic to the locally minimal orbits ... are dense in F , and on F , fH t|F has a dense orbit ?

accepted.question_text: Consider the spatial n-body problem with n ≥ 3 after fixing the center of mass at 0 and performing the paper's smooth time-reparametrization to obtain a complete flow generated by H_e on the energy surface H_e^{-1}(0). For every energy value e, is the nonwandering set of the Hamiltonian flow of H_e nowhere dense in H_e^{-1}(0)?

evidence.quote: 7.3 - Following G.D. Birkhoﬀ ... Question. Is for every e the non wandering set of the Hamiltonian ﬂow of He on H−1 e (0) nowhere dense in H−1 e (0) ?

needs_review.question_text_raw: The author has been unable to decide if this is also true when p = 1 !

evidence.quote: when n = 1 and α is of constant type ... Uα is open near 0, in the W 4,p, p> 1, topology. The author has been unable to decide if this is also true when p = 1 !

needs_review.question_text_raw: it is an open problem to prove, when n = 3, that Ec⊕Eu deﬁnes a C0-foliation !

evidence.quote: The answer is not even known if the dimension of Mn is n = 3. If Ec⊕Eu or Ec⊕Es deﬁnes aC0- foliation, it would follow that it is negative ... but it is an open problem to prove, when n = 3, that Ec⊕Eu deﬁnes aC0-foliation !

needs_review.question_text_raw: one wonders how bad Pεn behaves, when εn→ 1, in the space of compact sets on H−1 εn

evidence.quote: A theorem of Hofer and Zehnder [HZ] says that for εn→ 1, the Hamiltonian ﬂow ofH on H−1(εn) has at least one periodic orbit Pεn and one wonders how bad Pεn behaves, when εn→ 1, in the space of compact sets on H−1 εn .

needs_review.question_text_raw: when one mass is 1 and the others are εMj with ε small, are there wandering domains near distinct coplanar circular orbits around the large mass?

evidence.quote: What seems not an unreasonable question to ask ... is that : In one of the masses m0 = 1 and the other masses mj =εMj, 1≤j≤n−1, Mj > 0,ε>0, then in any neighbourhodd of ﬁxed diﬀerent circulator orbits arounds m0 moving in the same direction in a plane, when εis small, there are wandering domains.
